g.text: Correcting a Mistake, and Who Is Allowed to See It
PH-14-GRN-0003 recorded 120 m. The delivery note said 120,
the truck actually carried 100. The GRN is already signed,
already counted, already reported to the client.
stock back twice. A reversal is
Four rows now exist, and all four stay.
Balance is correct, *and* the audit trail still shows
that somebody booked 120, noticed, and corrected it -
with a name, a timestamp and a reason attached.
An UPDATE would have produced the same balance and
The same ledger, seen by a vendor
A requisition carries the engineer's internal
argument for *why* this material is needed and
*how much* the project can bear. A vendor reading
it is a vendor negotiating with your own cost
Unlike the punch list - where RLS mostly prevents
noise - here a leak has a price tag.
Verified live against the seeded fixture:
Lots and movements are readable by every project
participant but writable only by the custodian -
the client must be able to audit stock without
being able to book a receipt.
